## Assignments and Grading

Across the semester, you build **one dashboard** about a dataset you collect yourself. Each assignment adds a page to it. The final is the polished, published version.

| Assignment | Due | Points |
|------------|-----|--------|
| Participation (in-class activities) | Weekly | 10 |
| A1: GitHub account + Git installed | Feb 1 | 5 |
| Data proposal | Feb 16 | 5 |
| A2: The Data page | Mar 14 | 10 |
| Oral midterm (20 minutes, booked in office hours) | Week of Mar 15 | 25 |
| A3: What People Say page | Mar 29 | 10 |
| A4: Topics + Network page, published on GitHub | Apr 21 | 10 |
| Presentation | Apr 26 | 10 |
| Final dashboard | May 2 | 15 |
| **Total** | | **100** |

## Required Readings

### Session 1: Why Computational Social Science? {#readings-1}

- Hofman, J. M., Watts, D. J., Athey, S., Garip, F., Griffiths, T. L., Kleinberg, J., Margetts, H., Mullainathan, S., Salganik, M. J., Vazire, S., Vespignani, A., & Yarkoni, T. (2021). Integrating explanation and prediction in computational social science. *Nature*, 595(7866), 181-188. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03659-0

- Lazer, D. M. J., Pentland, A., Watts, D. J., Aral, S., Athey, S., Contractor, N., Freelon, D., Gonzalez-Bailon, S., King, G., Margetts, H., Nelson, A., Salganik, M. J., Strohmaier, M., Vespignani, A., & Wagner, C. (2020). Computational social science: Obstacles and opportunities. *Science*, 369(6507), 1060-1062. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaz8170

- Thulin, M. (2024). *Modern Statistics with R* - Chapter 2: The basics. Available at: https://www.modernstatisticswithr.com/thebasics.html

- Wickham, H., Çetinkaya-Rundel, M., & Grolemund, G. (2023). *R for Data Science* - Whole Game: Chapters 1-8. Available at: https://r4ds.hadley.nz/

**Additional readings for PhD students:**

- Peng, Y., Lu, Y., & Shen, C. (2023). An Agenda for Studying Credibility Perceptions of Visual Misinformation. *Political Communication*, 40(2), 225–237. https://doi.org/10.1080/10584609.2023.2175398

- Petchler, R., & González-Bailon, S. (2015). Automated content analysis of online political communication. In S. Coleman & D. Freelon (Eds.), *Handbook of Digital Politics* (pp. 433–450). Edward Elgar Publishing. https://doi.org/10.4337/9781782548768
